page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 server instance within the High Clock Speed family. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor offering a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The hardware layout comprises 20 physical cores, yielding 40 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by a 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB of RAM, equivalent to 4.8 GB per vCPU, paired with a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 12 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and does not feature dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the middle 50% across measured computational and memory domains. Its multi-threaded compute profile records a Geekbench multi-core score of 12045.0, a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95, and a stress-ng multi-core throughput of 38378.07. Extended vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI support operations such as software compilation via Clang (Geekbench sub-score of 28733.0) and ray tracing (29129.0). Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 108.89 GB/sec alongside 48.09 GB/sec in writes, facilitating in-memory operations like Redis SET throughput reaching 34.78 million operations per second.

The 4.8 GB-per-vCPU ratio situates this configuration between general-purpose and memory-focused allocations, balancing compute density and available memory per thread. Workloads reliant strictly on persistent internal storage require external cloud block storage attachments due to the absence of bundled local disks. This instance is technically suited for large-scale relational database engines, distributed caching layers, build pipelines, and enterprise enterprise web application hosting.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a High Clock Speed instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, it provides 40 dedicated vCPUs across 20 physical cores, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory and 12 Gbps of baseline networking. It contains no onboard local storage and lacks GPU accelerators. Standard benchmarks place its multi-core compute and memory transfer rates in the median tier, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 12045.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 108.89 GB/sec. Instruction support covers AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, contributing to solid performance in compilation and scientific workloads. The 4.8 GB memory-to-core density makes this server suitable for enterprise databases, in-memory key-value caching clusters, and mid-tier backend applications requiring consistent single-thread processor speeds.
